chapter: Chicago pioneers, community and New Orleans brotherhood
title: Elgar's death and New Orleans funeral in Chicago
summary: Elgar died at 94; Saunders, executor of his estate, gave him a New Orleans funeral with Jean Carroll singing, which the Tribune ignored.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Charles Elgar, is he still alive?
No. Mr. Elgar died about three years ago.
Yeah, I know he still had an ad in the Yellow Pages when I came to Chicago, --
-- because I was looking for a saxophone teacher for my son.
And I was surprised that he was still --
Yeah, he was still acting and he was teaching and then his hearing kind of went. He was 94 years old when he died, and we gave him a New Orleans funeral. I was the executor to his -- for his estate.
Uh-huh. And I was very close to him, I mean, I was like his son. And we gave him this New Orleans funeral, see, and we played him in and then we played him out.
And then Jean Carroll sang 'Just A Closer Walk With Thee,' beautiful. And then we did some tunes in the Catholic Church, with the mass. It was beautiful.
Now, if that happened in New Orleans, the Chicago Tribune would have run pictures of it.
Right. They knew about it, right.
